prior_implementation_evidence.durable_authority: A descriptor-confined owner-only macOS ledger binds root identity, key, lock, canonical signed state, generation, prior head, exact semantic effect, request, grant, expiry, recovery, settlement, and authenticated reuse witnesses.
prior_implementation_evidence.effect_binding: Protocol, context, candidate, plan, snapshot, result scope, and ordered intents are bound into the semantic effect identity before reservation.
prior_implementation_evidence.lifecycle: Fresh reservations move Reserved to Started before spawn and settle Complete, Failed, Cancelled, or Incomplete. Reserved and Started crashes expose only exact bounded recovery authority across process reopen.
prior_implementation_evidence.reuse: Completed effect artifacts are authenticated by the durable ledger. Exact reuse never falls back to spawning when the supplied artifact is absent or fails authentication.
prior_implementation_evidence.zero_write: No-op mediation bypasses authority initialization. Stale and self-inconsistent effect requests are rejected before authority files are initialized; help, read, query, and public dispatch remain outside this increment.
prior_implementation_evidence.store_security: The root must pre-exist as an owner-only 0700 directory. Key, lock, and state files must be owner-only regular single-link files. The owner-only file ledger detects unauthenticated state change and rollback relative to a live issuer. It is not an external monotonic anchor against a malicious account owner that can replace the complete key and signed store after all trusted process state is gone.
The post-operation invariant adds one bounded linear payload-validation pass per durable write; no performance benchmark claim is made.
The valid pre-boundary state constructor is cfg(test) only and does not create a production authority entrypoint.
